welcome.title: Colorado Tax Credit & Eligibility Estimator
welcome.subtitle: Find out how much you could receive in tax credits
welcome.description: Families with children in Colorado now have access to more tax credits than ever before! In 2025, families may receive between $2k and $10k per child in credits when filing their taxes. In less than 60 seconds, you can find out how much you could benefit by answering these simple questions.

howItWorks.step1: Answer a few quick questions about your family and income—it only takes seconds.
howItWorks.step2: Get an instant estimate of the tax credits you may qualify for.
howItWorks.step3: Start filing your taxes with ease.

married.title: Do you file taxes as single or jointly with a spouse?

children0To5.title: How many children under age 6 did you have at the end of 2025?
children0To5.description: Count kids who are 5 years old or younger as of December 31, 2025.

children6To16.title: How many children between the ages of 6 and 16 did you have at the end of 2025?
children6To16.description: Count kids who are 6 to 16 years old as of December 31, 2025.

hasIncome.title: Do you have an income?
hasIncome.titleWithSpouse: Do you or your spouse have an income?
hasIncome.description: We'll use this to estimate your tax credits.

incomeDetails.title: Tell us about your income
incomeDetails.description: We'll ask about each income source separately. You can add multiple incomes if you have more than one job.
incomeDetails.frequencyLabel: How often are you paid this income?
incomeDetails.amountLabel: How much do you receive before taxes each pay period for this income?
incomeDetails.hoursLabel: How many hours per week do you work?

careWorker.title: Do you regularly care for kids under 6 years old other than your own?
careWorker.description: Care workers include family, friends and neighbors who regularly care for kids under 6 years old (about 14 hours per week) in addition to licensed childcare providers, home health aides, personal care aides, and nursing assistants.

spouseCareWorker.title: Does your spouse regularly care for kids under 6 years old other than your own?
spouseCareWorker.description: Care workers include family, friends and neighbors who regularly care for kids under 6 years old (about 14 hours per week) in addition to licensed childcare providers, home health aides, personal care aides, and nursing assistants.

review.title: Let's review what you told us
review.description: Take a quick look to make sure everything looks right. You can always go back and change something!

coloradoCTC.eligible: You qualify for the Colorado Child Tax Credit based on your household information.
coloradoCTC.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Colorado Child Tax Credit based on your income and household size.

coloradoFATC.eligible: You qualify for the Colorado Family Affordability Tax Credit!
coloradoFATC.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Colorado Family Affordability Tax Credit based on your household situation.

coloradoEITC.eligible: You qualify for the Colorado EITC based on your earned income.
coloradoEITC.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Colorado EITC based on your income level.

coloradoCareWorker.eligible: You qualify for the Colorado Care Worker Tax Credit!
coloradoCareWorker.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Colorado Care Worker Tax Credit. This credit is for those who regularly care for children under 6.

federalCTC.eligible: You qualify for the Federal Child Tax Credit based on your household.
federalCTC.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Federal Child Tax Credit based on your household information.

federalEITC.eligible: You qualify for the Federal EITC based on your earned income and household size.
federalEITC.ineligible: You may not qualify for the Federal EITC based on your income and household information.

results.disclaimer: These are estimates to help you plan. Your actual tax credits might be different based on your final tax return. Tax situations can be complex, so we always recommend talking with a tax professional or using official IRS and Colorado Department of Revenue resources when you file.

errors.validation: Please fill in all income fields. For hourly income, enter both the hourly rate and hours per week.

filingQuiz.title: Find the Best Way to File Your Taxes
filingQuiz.subtitle: Answer a few questions to get personalized recommendations
filingQuiz.intro: Free, in-person tax help will be limited in 2026. The good news is that you may be able to file your taxes online for free, with step-by-step help, and get your refund faster. Answer a few simple questions below to see if online filing is a good option for you.

computerComfort.title: On a scale of 1-5, how comfortable do you feel using a computer? (with 1 being the least comfortable and 5 being the most comfortable)

taxComfort.title: On a scale of 1-5, how comfortable do you feel about filing your own taxes? (with 1 being the least comfortable and 5 being the most comfortable)

lifeEvents.title: Have you experienced one of these four life changing events in the past year? (Select all that apply)

options.birthOrAdoption: Birth or adoption of a child

received1099.title: Did you fill out a W9 to receive payment and/or did you receive a 1099?

taxIdType.title: Do you have a social security number or are you filing with an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)?

filingYear.title: Are you filing only for the 2025 tax year or are you filing for a different year or multiple years?

languageAssistance.title: Do you need assistance in a language other than English or Spanish?
